title: Ulyana and the Contact
premise: Astrid Montrose, a veteran hostage negotiator haunted by the one call that ended in blood, is pulled into an impossible case: a private jet carrying a whistleblower has vanished from every radar, manifest, and memory mid-flight, as if it never existed. The plane's passenger was carrying proof of an inheritance scheme that launders power through generations of political dynasties, and Astrid realizes their own late mother's name appears in the ledger. As the summit convenes and the people who erased the flight close in, Astrid must negotiate with the one man who can restore the record — the fixer who once taught them every rule they now must break. In the end, Astrid trades the ledger for the whistleblower's life, exposes the scheme at the summit through a hostage negotiation broadcast live, and walks away stripped of career but finally free of the old failure.
about_author: Yara Sandoval is a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to strangers talk each other back from the edge. She writes thrillers about people who discover that institutions are just stories we agreed to believe.

chapters.title: The Empty Board
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Twenty years after the Kessler call went wrong, Astrid trains new negotiators by day and drinks alone by night. A summons arrives: Flight 447 to Geneva has vanished — not crashed, vanished — from every system while still airborne. Emotional beat: numb routine cracked open by a mystery that feels personally aimed at them.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Digging into the passenger list, Astrid finds names scrubbed in real time as they watch, including their own mother's. A survivor — the whistleblower's daughter, Lena — surfaces in a safehouse, terrified. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion; the past was never buried, only filed.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Astrid and Marek Voss, the fixer. Flashbacks reveal Voss trained Astrid, and that he orchestrated the erasure to protect the consortium's heirs before the summit. Each begins maneuvering the other. Emotional beat: mentor and student circling, respect sharpened into threat.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Lena decrypts part of the ledger: inheritances traded like currency, judges and ministers bound by debts older than their careers. Astrid finds their mother listed not as victim but as architect. Emotional beat: betrayal; the family myth collapses, and justice starts to feel like inheritance too.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Lena. The safehouse is compromised; Lena counts exits while Astrid stalls the incoming 'security team' by phone, buying minutes with pure technique. They escape with half the ledger. Emotional beat: Astrid's skill reborn as something righteous instead of institutional.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Voss offers Astrid reinstatement, protection, and a clean version of the Kessler file — in exchange for Lena and the ledger. Astrid recognizes the shape of the deal: it's the same bargain their mother took. Emotional beat: temptation rendered almost reasonable, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Instead of surrendering, Astrid leaks a fragment of the ledger to three rival factions inside the consortium, turning its own heirs against each other days before the summit. Emotional beat: cold exhilaration — Astrid stops negotiating within the rules and starts negotiating the rules themselves.

chapters.title: Flight Path
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. It emerges Flight 447 landed at a private strip; the whistleblower is alive, held as insurance. Voss, betrayed by his own principals, sends Astrid the coordinates — a defection disguised as a trap. Emotional beat: the student becomes the leverage; loyalty rerouted.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Astrid takes the summit's security room hostage — negotiator turned captor — and forces a live broadcast, walking the delegates through the ledger on air while stalling the response team with the same techniques that failed at Kessler. Emotional beat: climax; every old failure repurposed into precision.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. The whistleblower testifies; arrests ripple outward; Voss surrenders the full archive and asks Astrid to say he taught them well. Astrid declines the job offer that follows, hands Lena the original ledger, and finally closes the Kessler file. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — justice delivered outside the law, inheritance refused.
